question: Will US and Iranian negotiators meet in person in November or December 2026?

calls.reasoning: Base rate: 4 in-person rounds over ~8 months of war (Apr, Jun, Jul, Sep), so 3 of the 4 two-month windows from April to October had one; October had none. Status quo as of Nov 3: indirect Qatar/Pakistan proposal exchange, Araghchi (Oct 31) saying there is 'no need to meet with the Americans at this stage', Rezaei rejecting a direct-contact plan in Doha, and Trump threatening post-midterm strikes. On the other side: Vance's written offer to lead a delegation to Qatar/Turkiye, the Supreme Leader empowering the government to accelerate talks, Iran's accelerated 2-day Hormuz plan, and any deal likely needing a signing meeting; a shuttle within one venue also counts. Polymarket's similar 'diplomatic meeting by Dec 31' was ~41.5% on Nov 1 (contract wording slightly different: direct or indirect talks between senior officials, same-venue requirement unverified). Landing a bit above the market because the window is 58 days long and the shuttle format counts.
calls.dossier:
- Prior in-person rounds (question background): Islamabad Apr 11-12; Burgenstock Jun 21-28; Doha Jul 1-2; New York Sep 22 (Qatari PM shuttling between teams, which counts). None reported in October.
- Oct 31 2026 (Rio Times): Iranian FM Araghchi said Tehran saw 'no need to meet with the Americans at this stage'; conditions clear, mediators consulting. Iranian conditions: lift naval blockade, sanctions relief, oil waivers, release of frozen assets in Qatar, guaranteed end to strikes, regional ceasefire including Lebanon.
- ~Oct 25-30 (Iran International, Al Jazeera, EA WorldView): VP Vance sent a letter via Qatar to SNSC Secretary Mohsen Rezaei offering to lead a US delegation in direct talks, possibly 'as soon as next week in Qatar or Turkiye', with the nuclear program on the table from the outset. Iranian officials reportedly received it positively, but Iran insists nuclear talks come after a Hormuz/sanctions deal.
- Late Oct (newsquawk/Aram News, jfeed): Rezaei rejected a Qatari proposal for direct communication between US diplomats and the Iranian delegation that visited Doha.
- Nov 1-3 (Al Jazeera, CBS, azat.tv): Qatar and Pakistan facilitating 'real-time exchange of proposals'; three days of indirect closed-door talks, no breakthrough; venue/co-location not reported. Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei granted the government powers to accelerate talks; Iran proposed shortening implementation to 2 days (US measures day 1, Hormuz reopens day 2). Trump signals progress, says a deal is still possible.
- Nov 2-3 (CBS): US 'limited defensive strikes' on Qeshm Island after IRGC fire at a US aircraft; Trump camp threatened strikes from Nov 4 (after the midterms); Iran's Supreme Leader warned of 'no geographical limitations'.
- Qatari mediators expected feedback on new proposals within 36h of Nov 3.
- Status quo: indirect, mediator-carried exchanges with no US and Iranian negotiators in the same venue. Qatari trips to Tehran do NOT count (no US negotiator present).
- Base rate: 4 in-person rounds over ~8 months of war, so 3 of the 4 two-month windows from Apr to Oct had at least one; the most recent ~6 weeks (late Sep to Nov 3) had none.
- Resolution instrument: resolves on credible reports of a US exec-branch negotiator and an Iranian government negotiator in the same venue (shuttle mediation in one venue counts), not on phone/letter exchanges or mediator trips.
- Event window: Nov 1 2026 -> Dec 31 2026 per the criteria; as of Nov 3 about 5% elapsed.
- Human market exists (Polymarket 'US x Iran diplomatic meeting by...'): its wording counts direct or indirect talks between senior officials/envoys; full rules not retrieved, so it is unclear whether it requires the same venue.
- Searched but not found: any scheduled date/venue for a new round; any Kalshi or Manifold contract.
calls.reference_class: Two-month windows during the 2026 US-Iran war (Apr-Oct 2026) that contained an in-person US-Iran negotiating round

calls.reasoning: Base rate: since Feb 2026 in-person rounds (incl. shuttle formats) occurred in Apr, Jun, Jul, Sep — nearly every 2-month window contained one, though Oct had none. As of Nov 3, Qatar-mediated indirect talks are intense (Iranian delegation in Doha Oct 30–Nov 1, Vance letter called 'positive' by Araghchi, reports of US delegation expected in Doha and a possible Doha/Istanbul meeting within a week), but Araghchi says no need to meet Americans now, Rezaei reportedly blocked direct talks, and Trump threatens strikes after Nov 3 midterms. Question counts same-venue shuttle diplomacy (looser than direct), so I put it above Polymarket's ~42% for a 'US x Iran diplomatic meeting by Dec 31' (Nov 1). I couldn't confirm that contract's terms, so I treat it as a lower bound, not an anchor.

- Count: of seven 2-month windows Mar-Apr through Sep-Oct 2026, all seven contained at least one in-person round; by single month, 4 of 8 months (Mar–Oct) had one.
- Oct 30, 2026: Qatari mediation delegation held 12+ hours of talks in Tehran; Iranian delegation (incl. Araghchi aide / deputy FM) traveled to Doha the next day (Al Jazeera Oct 31; The New Arab Oct 31).
- Oct 31: The New Arab/Al-Araby reported a US delegation was 'expected to join' Iranian officials in Doha after a 'breakthrough', but no arrival date was set. EA WorldView cited reports of a possible meeting within a week in Doha or Istanbul.
- Oct 31: Araghchi: 'We see no need to meet with the Americans at this stage'; called a Vance letter proposing talks a 'positive step'; said reports of upcoming meetings were 'media speculation' (Al Jazeera Oct 31). Nov 3: Araghchi denied an agreement to hold direct talks in Qatar, Turkey or elsewhere.
- ImArabic report: Mohsen Rezaei blocked a Qatari plan for direct US-Iran meetings in Doha; it mentions 'US diplomats whose presence in the Qatari capital coincided' with the talks (unnamed, unconfirmed; no credible outlet frames it as a US-Iran meeting).
- Nov 1-2: Iranian negotiators left Doha after ~3 days of Qatari-mediated talks; an official said a follow-up is possible and the departure was not a breakdown. A draft proposal is circulating, and Qatar expected both sides to respond within 36 hours (Reuters via investing.com; Washington Times Nov 1).
- Nov 2: Trump signals progress; Iran pushes accelerated 7-step plan (reopen Hormuz in 2 days for blockade lift, sanctions relief, end of strikes); Iran refuses to negotiate on nuclear program (Al Jazeera Nov 2).
- Trump said strikes could come after the Nov 3 midterms ('brief but intense', as early as Nov 4); US conducted limited 'defensive' strikes near Hormuz on the eve of the elections (CBS, EA WorldView).
- June 2026 MoU (Doha/Islamabad) collapsed in August, a precedent for deals breaking down.
- Resolution: same-venue presence of authorized US exec and Iranian govt negotiators reported as talks; shuttle mediation in the same venue counts. Resolves off credible reporting, not official joint statements.
- Event window: Nov 1, 2026 -> Dec 31, 2026 per the criteria; as of Nov 3, 2026, ~5% elapsed.
- Human market: Polymarket 'US x Iran diplomatic meeting by Dec 31, 2026' exists (multi-million $ volume event); its contract terms on indirect/shuttle formats were not confirmed. Its rules may be stricter than this question's. No Kalshi or bookmaker market checked or found.
- Searched but not found: confirmed arrival of named US negotiators in Doha after Oct 31; any scheduled date for a next round.

calls.reasoning: Base rate: four same-venue US-Iran rounds since Feb 2026 (Apr, Jun, Jul, Sep), so most two-month windows had one, though October had none. As of Nov 3 talks are indirect via Qatar/Pakistan. Araghchi denies any planned meeting, Rezaei blocked Qatar's direct-talks plan, and post-midterm US strikes are threatened. For yes: Vance's offer to lead a delegation (which Iran called positive), Iran's accelerated plan, Qatar pushing proximity talks, a likely in-person signing for any deal, 58 days of window, and same-venue shuttle talks counting. Polymarket's Dec 31 'senior meeting' contract has risen to ~50%. This question's criteria are probably looser, so I land slightly above it.
calls.reconciliation: The runs disagreed mainly on how to weigh Iran's refusal against the momentum toward talks, and on how to use the Polymarket price. Checks: (1) Polymarket's Dec 31 contract is now ~49-51c ($493k on that date, $1.26M on the event), up from the 41.5% the runs cited for Nov 1; Nov 30 is ~31c. The full rules weren't visible, so whether shuttle talks count is still unknown. (2) News search: there is still no confirmed US delegation arrival or scheduled round. Araghchi said on Nov 1-3 that no meeting is planned and denied an agreement on direct talks in Qatar or Türkiye. Reports of a US delegation 'expected' in Doha are still unconfirmed. (3) I also searched for a Kalshi or bookmaker market and found none. The market's rise supports the higher runs. This question's looser criteria (any authorized negotiator, shuttle in the same venue) put it at or a bit above the market. The escalation risk from Nov 4 and Iran's explicit refusal keep it well below the base rate.
